mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 12-month average when FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS up > 10,000 and UNRATE down > 0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to outperform the 30-day moving average during periods of strong labor indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% y/y for two consecutive months predicts a shift in investor expectations toward higher future growth, resulting in positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL meeting the growth threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% while the S&P 500 20-day forward return remains flat or negative indicates overproduction, which suppresses equity valuations and yields negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth reverses direction or 20-day returns turn positive during periods of weak production.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 2% for three consecutive months during a non-recessionary regime, the discount rate premium embedded in equity pricing is expected to compress, generating positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE < 4.5%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive when the low-rate condition persists beyond 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-standard-deviation increase in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) followed by a sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates expectations of wage growth and reduced labor market tightness, which can drive negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors price in higher inflation and slower growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS up > +10,000 and UNRATE down > -0.2% in the same month, followed by UNRATE below 5% the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not turn positive within 30 days of the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in personal consumption (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 1% y/y for two consecutive months in the absence of a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests robust consumer demand that outpaces supply, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 1% for 2 months and INDPRO flat or down
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative when demand accelerates without corresponding supply response.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative regardless of labor or supply indicators, indicating that rate hikes dominate equity pricing behavior in this regime.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during the identified tightening regime.
